messages:
maria: FYI canary for release 2026.4 started failing after 8m, error spike on /generate. tagging for rollback discussion. https://go/runbooks/helm-canary
deploy-bot: Canary check failed: metric=error_rate threshold=0.5% observed=1.8% window=5m. canary_id=canary-2026-4-3
kevin: logs look like model-serving 503s, 95th latency jumped. looks tied to chart v1.13.0 image update?
leo: It's the values change that increased batch size to 64 — might be saturating the worker pool. we should consider pinning to v1.12.3 while we investigate.
maria: agree. quick decision: rollback to chart v1.12.3 and revert values.batchSize -> 32. can someone run a rollback and update release notes? cc @kevin
ops-sre: confirm no schema/db migration in this chart? if there was a migration we should instead hotpatch.
kevin: no migrations, just worker/retry config and image tag. safe to rollback.
leo: running helm rollback now. command:
```
helm upgrade inference-service redwood/inference --version 1.12.3 -f values-prod.yaml --namespace prod --reuse-values
```
maria: also pin chart in the release bundle so deploy-bot won't auto-upgrade this app next window. add `chartVersion: 1.12.3` to release metadata.
deploy-bot: Observed deployment failure pattern: rollingRestart pods OOMKilled during canary -> suggests increased memory per batch. Registered fallback policy: pin_chart and scale-down-batch. Applying pin if approved.
kevin: approved. apply pin and post minimal release note: "Reverted worker batch/worker concurrency change; pinned chart 1.12.3 pending follow-up investigation."
maria: make sure to include the change window note: "Out of change window rollback during incident — will schedule formal patch in next window." add link to ticket: https://issues/redwood/INFR-4321
leo: pushed pin and rollback succeeded. pods are back to Ready=3/3. canary monitoring shows error_rate down to 0.12% in the last 3m.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete. canary_id=canary-2026-4-3 status=rolled_back to 1.12.3. pinned chart in manifest. notify=eng-release,ops
maria: thanks. next steps: create a short postmortem bullet list + test matrix for batchSize=64 locally before reintroducing. assigning action items in INFR-4321.
kevin: i'll draft release note blurb and keep the change small on next attempt. :thumbsup:
ops-sre: also set a lower canary concurrency cap for the next run so we don't risk infra saturation.
maria: good call. closing this thread. will follow up in the ticket with timelines.
